mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate tighter policy, causing a short-term discounting effect that depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the next month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening window (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS rise is ≤0.25pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.3% over two consecutive months signals deflationary expectations, prompting risk-on sentiment and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are negative or not statistically superior to baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL decline is <0.3% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 jobs per month triggers optimism about economic resilience, which amplifies equity valuation multiples and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 in the following 20 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05), or PAYEMS does not exceed 200,000 in the specified window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 5% in a single month indicates accelerating supply-side momentum, which reduces near-term discounting and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥5% in one month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over 60 days are not significantly positive (IC < 0.05), or INDPRO increase is <5%.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent weakness in retail sales (HOUST) below 1,600 thousand units for two consecutive months suggests consumer demand softening, which elevates risk aversion and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST remains below 1,600 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 5-day horizon are not negative (t-test p > 0.05), or HOUST recovers above 1,600 within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals tight labor markets, which can trigger wage-price spirals and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% over the next 20 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (IC < 0.10), or UNRATE does not fall below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% create expectations of lower future rate hikes, which reduces discounting and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL remains below 2.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over 60 days are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL rises above 2.0% in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence proxies (combined via a composite index from available series) show simultaneous strength, this interaction signals dual momentum that amplifies equity valuation and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 110 and GDPC1 > 12,000 in the next 20 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (IC < 0.05), or the two proxies do not move in the required direction simultaneously.
